name: Steady
vehicle: S&P 500 index ETF, no leverage (UCITS, e.g. iShares Core S&P 500)
rule: Buy every week using the €40–200 rule. Never sell on signals; ride out crashes.
worst_case: About −50% in a 2008-type crash; recovery took ~5 years

name: Growth
vehicle: 2x daily-leveraged S&P 500 ETF (e.g. Xtrackers S&P 500 2x Leveraged Daily Swap)
rule: Hold the 2x ETF only while the S&P 500 closes the week above its 200-day average. If a Friday close is below it, sell all of it and hold cash or a money-market fund; buy back after the first Friday close above. Weekly money follows the same rule.
worst_case: −50% to −60% if a crash hits faster than one weekly check (e.g. October 1987 style)

name: Aggressive
vehicle: 3x daily-leveraged S&P 500 ETP (e.g. WisdomTree S&P 500 3x Daily Leveraged)
rule: Same weekly 200-day rule as the 20% plan, with the 3x product. Below the line: sell everything, hold cash.
worst_case: −70% or worse; a single −33% day would wipe out a 3x product
